comment: Local mutation testing for the GENERATOR — proves the high-coverage generator files are backed by KILLING assertions, not just executed lines. Run via scripts/housekeeping.ps1 -Mutation (needs: dotnet tool install -g dotnet-stryker --version 4.16.0). MEASURED 2026-08-19 on Stryker 4.16.0, against the WHOLE test suite (5,798 tests discovered), 12 logical cores, on an otherwise QUIET machine (~2 % CPU and no concurrent build at launch): score 71.64 % (144 detected of 201 scoreable — 144 killed, 0 timeout; 46 survived, 11 uncovered, 42 in-scope compile errors excluded), 21 min 02 s wall-clock. break is that score rounded DOWN to 71. THIS IS THE LEG'S FIRST COMPLETED RUN: the previous break of 70 was INHERITED AND HAD NEVER BEEN MEASURED — 'comment' sat INSIDE the 'stryker-config' object until 2026-08-16 (Stryker 4.16 rejects unknown keys there and refuses to run at all, 'the allowed keys for the "stryker-config" object are {...} but "comment" was found'), and the 'mutate' globs were repo-root-relative until the same day, which matches nothing and produces a VACUOUS run that still exits 0. That 70 happens to pass today; it was a coincidence, not evidence. NOTE 1 — 71.64 % IS THE HONEST NUMBER AND 72.64 % MUST NOT BE 'RESTORED'. The first completed run, with no 'additional-timeout', scored 72.64 % (146/201) in 22 min 01 s. Two of those 'detections' were TIMEOUTS, and both are provably incapable of hanging: BlittableProof.cs L28 turns 'if (!a.IsUnmanagedType || !b.IsUnmanagedType)' into '&&' — no loop, and LayoutIdentical only recurses through STRUCT fields, where C# forbids a cycle (CS0523), so the depth is finite — and L58 flips one 'or' to 'and' inside IsPrimitive's pattern, a single enum pattern match with no loop at all. This is the exact defect stryker-config.runtime.json documents: Stryker computes 'total timeout = initialTestTime + additional-timeout', the initial serial run of this suite measures ~3 min 23 s here (203 s), and the default cushion is a handful of seconds, so the ceiling sits just above the workload. It fires under load, and Stryker COUNTS A TIMEOUT AS DETECTED. THE FIX IS THE CLOCK, NOT THE COVERAGE: 'additional-timeout' is 120000 ms. Both mutants then resolve honestly as Survived, ZERO mutants gained detection, and the whole 1.00 pp delta is those two re-classifications. NOTE 2 — WHY THIS LEG IS SLOW, AND WHY IT MUST NOT BE MADE FAST BY FILTERING. 85 of the 201 scoreable mutants are STATIC ('static': true in the report), so Stryker cannot attribute per-test coverage to them and each one re-runs the ENTIRE 5,798-test suite. That is ~493,000 test executions against ~1,580 for every covered mutant put together: the static set IS the cost. Per file, static of scoreable: ConstructorSelector 50/87, BlittableProof 27/88, LocationInfo 5/5, EquatableArray 3/21. No 'test-case-filter' and no 'test-projects' key appear here, deliberately — the maintainer ruled test-set exclusion out for the runtime leg and the ruling binds here; stryker-config.runtime.json measures why an exclusive test list drifts in the one direction nothing catches. If this leg gets slower, raise 'additional-timeout' or lower its frequency; do not narrow what it tests. NOTE 3 — the 'mutate' globs must be PROJECT-relative ('**/Name.cs'), never repo-root-relative: Stryker resolves them against src/DwarfMapper.Generator, so 'src/DwarfMapper.Generator/Foo.cs' matches nothing, every mutant is dropped with 'Removed by mutate filter', and Stryker STILL EXITS 0. Assert-MutantsWereTested (scripts/housekeeping.ps1) exists for exactly that hazard; it counts scoreable statuses in the JSON report and returns 201 for this run. NOTE 4 — Stryker mutates and COMPILES the whole project regardless of these globs (11,389 mutants created; 7,016 dropped by the mutate filter; 4,142 rolled back as compile errors; 30 dropped by the block-already-covered filter; 190 tested plus 11 uncovered), and only then filters what is TESTED. So the report contains every file in the project, and the four named here are the only ones carrying scoreable statuses — that is the non-vacuity check to make. The whole-project compile is also why ~6 minutes pass before the first mutant is tested. NOTE 5 — there is deliberately NO 'test-projects' key. It would be INERT: Stryker discovers the solution and enumerates EVERY test project in it, so such a list does not select the test set (see NOTE 3 in stryker-config.runtime.json for the measurement that established this). It was removed rather than corrected, so nothing here pretends to scope anything. NOTE 6 — the 46 survivors and 11 uncovered mutants are catalogued, with a real-hole-or-equivalent judgement for each, in Issues/ledgers/T3-mutation-survivors.md. Raise break only by killing survivors.
